Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ITU-based estimates (Digital Watch Observatory and a 2025 academic field survey using ARPT/ITU data) put national 4G/LTE population coverage at roughly 75-78% (2023), consistent with the 75-89% band. Coverage is concentrated on the Orange network; MTN and Cellcom lag significantly outside Conakry, so rural coverage is materially lower than the national figure implies.

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: Single IXP (IXP-GUINEE) operational since 2018, limited participation. [Data Center Map](https://www.datacentermap.com/ixp/internet-exchange-point-of-guinea/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. IXP-GUINEE, founded March 2018 and operating two nodes in Conakry, remains the country's single, limited-participation exchange point per Digital Watch Observatory's current country profile. Code 3 stands.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Human review flagged: the variable requires unique subscriber penetration, but the cited 95.1% (and a newer Digital 2026 figure of 84.6%, late 2025) are GSMA 'connections' (SIM) data, which typically overstate unique-subscriber penetration given widespread multi-SIM ownership. No GSMA Intelligence unique-subscriber percentage specific to Guinea could be located; true unique-subscriber penetration could plausibly sit in either the 55-69% (code 4) or 70%+ (code 5) band. Not changed pending a primary GSMA unique-subscriber figure.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Enacted law L/2016/037/AN on Cybersecurity and Personal Data Protection, DPA not yet established. [DLA Piper](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?t=law&c=GN)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Score corrected. Law L/2016/037/AN (28 July 2016) establishes a comprehensive data protection regime, but the dedicated Data Protection Authority (APDP) mandated by its Article 47 remains unestablished: a draft law to formally create the APDP was still before the National Transition Council in 2024, and an April 2025 decree addressed only data-security conditions, not the authority itself. The original comment already flagged 'DPA not yet established', which contradicts code 4 (requires DPA established) — corrected to code 3 (legislation enacted but no enforcement authority).

Definition: The presence and tier quality of commercial/colocation data center facilities operating in the country. Commercial data centers provide the physical infrastructure for hosting cloud services, content delivery, and enterprise applications domestically.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed. GUILAB's Conakry facility (Centre Emetteur de Kipé, ~229m2 across pylon, meet-me-room and colocation spaces) remains the only identified commercial data centre in Guinea; no Tier III/IV or hyperscale operator (e.g. Raxio, active elsewhere in Africa but not in Guinea) was found. Small-scale Tier I-II, code 2 stands (current as of 2024-25 per operator site).
